title: Cafe-Talk: Generating 3D Talking Face Animation with Multimodal Coarse- and Fine-grained Control

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to achieve the first speech-driven 3D talking face generation system with coarse-to-fine multimodal conditional control (effective, precise, flexible). Several prior papers address related objectives but none explicitly combine coarse-grained (e.g., talking style/emotion labels/intensity) and fine-grained (e.g., AU sequences) conditional control in a unified framework. For example:
- Paper [5] ("3D-TalkEmo") focuses on synthesizing 3D talking heads with rich emotions but does not incorporate fine-grained AU-level control alongside coarse-grained emotion labels.
- Paper [7] ("EmoVOCA") blends speech-related motions with expression dynamics but does not explicitly address hierarchical coarse-to-fine control.
- Paper [24] ("Efficient Emotional Adaptation") introduces emotion-controllable talking-head generation but focuses on adapting emotion-agnostic models rather than hierarchical multimodal control.
Thus, no prior paper achieves the same purpose at the problem-class level.

### Mechanism
The contribution mechanism is a diffusion-transformer-based generative model (Cafe-Talk) that integrates coarse-grained conditions (e.g., talking style/emotion labels/intensity encoded via CLIP) and fine-grained conditions (e.g., AU sequences). Several prior papers use diffusion models or transformers for speech-driven 3D talking face generation, but none combine coarse-grained and fine-grained multimodal conditions in this specific way:
- Paper [17] ("DiT-Head") uses diffusion transformers for high-resolution talking head synthesis but does not incorporate hierarchical coarse-to-fine multimodal conditions.
- Paper [20] ("DiffSpeaker") aggregates diffusion models and transformers but does not address coarse-to-fine multimodal conditional control.
- Paper [16] ("SAiD") employs diffusion models for speech-driven 3D facial animation but focuses on blendshape animation rather than hierarchical multimodal conditions.
- Paper [29] ("Region Based Adversarial Synthesis") introduces AU-level facial expression synthesis but does not integrate coarse-grained conditions like talking style or emotion labels.
Thus, the mechanism is novel.

### Evaluation
The contribution evaluates lip synchronization (LVE/SyncNet) and expression generation (Acc/Div) on MEAD/RAVDESS datasets, comparing against SOTA methods, and conducts a 38-person user study assessing naturalness, expressiveness, and lip-sync quality. Several prior papers use similar evaluation designs:
- Paper [5] ("3D-TalkEmo") evaluates emotion synthesis using synchronized audio-video datasets and objective metrics like accuracy and diversity.
- Paper [17] ("DiT-Head") compares lip-sync quality and visual fidelity against SOTA methods using similar benchmarks.
- Paper [24] ("Efficient Emotional Adaptation") conducts user studies to assess expressiveness and naturalness.
The evaluation design (benchmark comparison and user study) is covered.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of 3D talking face animation generation. This domain is extensively addressed by prior papers:
- Paper [5] ("3D-TalkEmo") focuses on audio-driven 3D talking head synthesis with emotional expression.
- Paper [7] ("EmoVOCA") blends speech-driven motions with expression dynamics for 3D talking heads.
- Paper [17] ("DiT-Head") synthesizes high-resolution 3D talking heads using diffusion transformers.
Thus, the domain is covered.
